questions.stemHtml: Identify the nerve passing around the marked structure :
questions.solutionHtml:
Common Peroneal Nerve

Structure marked is the neck of fibula , a common peroneal nerve passes around it.

Common Peroneal nerve

  • The most common presentation with common peroneal nerve injury or palsy is acute foot drop.



Gray’s Anatomy 42nd Edition, Page No. 1415.

questions.stem: Incorrect match about the pharyngeal arch artery derivative?1st arch- maxillary artery2nd arch- hyoid and stapedial artery3rd arch- common carotid and proximal part of ICA4th arch- right subclavian artery6th arch- Aorta on the left sideChoose the correct answer from below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
5

The proximal part of the sixth right arch persists as the proximal part of the right pulmonary artery while the distal section degenerates;

The sixth left arch gives off the left pulmonary artery and forms the ductus arteriosus; this duct remains pervious during the whole of fetal life, but then closes within the first few days after birth due to increased O2 concentration. Oxygen concentration causes the production of bradykinin which causes the ductus to constrict, occluding all flow. Within 1–3 months, the ductus is obliterated and becomes the ligamentum arteriosum.



Langman's Medical Embryology , 14th Edition, Page No. 208.

questions.stem: Which of the muscles make the pelvic diaphragm?Deep Transverse PerineiPubococcygeusIliococcygeusObturator InternusChoose the correct options from below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
b, c

Levator ani muscle is a complex unit that consists of 3 muscle components:

  • Pubococcygeus
    • Pubovaginalis
    • Pub Perinealis
    • Puboanalis
  • Puborectalis
  • Iliococcygeus
  • Levator ani muscles are the most important muscles in the pelvic floor and maintain a constant state of contraction.
  • Major function of the levator ani muscle is supporting and raising the pelvic visceral structures. It also helps in proper sexual functioning, defecation, urination, and allowing various structures to pass through it


Shaw Textbook of Gynecology, 16th Edition, Page No. 514.

questions.stem: A hyperkinetic involuntary movement disorder characterized by intermittent, sudden, violent, involuntary, flinging, or ballistic high amplitude movements of upper limb, known as hemiballismus is due to which part involvement:
questions.solutionHtml:
Subthalamic Nucleus
  • Hemiballismus is a hyperkinetic involuntary movement disorder characterized by intermittent, sudden, violent, involuntary, flinging, or ballistic high amplitude movements involving the ipsilateral arm and leg caused by dysfunction in the central nervous system of the contralateral side.
  • Hemiballismus is usually caused by a stroke that affects a small area just below the basal ganglia called the subthalamic nucleus. The subthalamic nucleus helps control voluntary movements.


Gray’s Anatomy for Students, 4th Edition, Page No: 1428.

questions.stemHtml: Actions of the muscle attached to the marked area of the bone?
questions.solutionHtml:
Extension and Lateral rotation
  • The marked area is Gluteal Tuberosity
  • The muscle inserted to the gluteal tuberosity is Gluteus maximus
  • Action of gluteus maximus is extension and lateral rotation of the hip.


Gray’s Anatomy, 4th Edition, Page No. 570.
